A demonstrator aligned with the <e>Europ:
A demonstrator aligned with the European Health Data Space Regulation, built on Eclipse EDC 1.0, Neo4j, FHIR R4 and OMOP CDM. CFM and the DCore data planes run only in the stack's

edc018 profile

(ADR-078). A 5-layer knowledge graph carries the Regulation's data, from DSP marketplace discovery to ontology alignment, for sovereign health data exchange between data holders and approved research users. Explore the architecture →
Security and data protection are tested: Security and data protection are tested by the project itself with tools anyone can run on the repository, and every finding is either fixed or named as open. The test of 2026-10-15 found ten findings, F1 to F10: after the fixes nine are closed and one is reviewed and accepted (F3, the published development default key of the local compose stack; Azure takes its keys from Vault). None of this is an independent penetration test or a certification. How the platform is operated for real, role by role, is the operational guideline in the Operations section.

Klarbefund is the iPhone app of this pro: Klarbefund is the iPhone app of this project. It scans a paper lab report, reads the values on the device, codes them with <loinc>LOINC</loinc>, keeps them encrypted on the phone and exports them as <fhir>FHIR</fhir> and <omop>OMOP</omop>, or sends them to the person's own record on the hub when they say so. The European Health Data Space is <e>Reg:
The European Health Data Space is Regulation (EU) 2025/327. This section says what the integration hub implements of it, article by article: the page, the route or the file that does it, the test that shows it, and where it falls short, with the issue that tracks the gap. Article numbers are the adopted ones; older material in the repository may still cite the

2022 proposal

, and the numbering page maps one to the other.

Regulation (EU) 2025/327 applies in stag: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 applies in stages (<art>Art. 105</art>): generally from 26 March 2027, secondary use in full from 26 March 2029, further data categories from 26 March 2031. The 2026 implementing acts turn articles into specifications: dataset descriptions (<a98>2026/2098</a98>), cross-border identification and authentication of persons and health professionals, with assurance levels (<a99>2026/2099</a99>), MyHealth@EU (<a83>2026/2083</a83>).
Simpl, the EU's data space middleware: Simpl, the EU's data space middleware
Simpl-Open is the Commission's open-sour: Simpl-Open is the Commission's open-source middleware for European data spaces; the EHDS secondary-use data space is one of the six data spaces of <w1>Simpl-Live wave 1</w1>. The hub meets it as a connector outside its agent, over <dsp>DSP</dsp> and <dcp>DCP</dcp>, and keeps the health rules in its own extension (<adr>ADR-064</adr>).
eIDAS 2.0: the EUDI Wallet and the Busin: eIDAS 2.0: the EUDI Wallet and the Business Wallet
<eidas>eIDAS 2.0</eidas> obliges every M: <eidas>eIDAS 2.0</eidas> obliges every Member State to offer a wallet. <a99>2026/2099, Art. 4(2)</a99> asks, for an online request through MyHealth@EU, for electronic identification means under eIDAS at assurance level substantial from 26 March 2027 and high from 26 March 2030; it does not single out the EUDI Wallet. The German wallet <dyou>d-you</dyou> is to be available from early 2027. The <ebw>European Business Wallet</ebw>, still in negotiation, lets a person act for an organisation, as a researcher applying for a permit does.
